newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian govt security prices rise on easy liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indian govt security prices rise on easy liquidity.

text.p: Indian government securities were up in active late morning Tuesday trade and dealers said they expect prices to remain firm during the day.
They said demand for securities had picked up from Monday's dull trade on lower call money rates.
Call money was traded at 3.5 percent on Tuesday against Monday's closing 4.75-5.25 percent.
"Security prices are up today... this is normal when call goes down," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Prices should remain firm today but I do not think they will go up much further."
In latest deals, the 12.59 percent 2004 stock traded between 104.14 and 104.18 rupees against Monday's 103.70-103.84, dealers said.
The 12 percent 1999 rose to 104.50 from 104.40 while the 13.50 percent 1998 edged up to 104.03 against 103.95.
The 13.05 percent 2007 long bond was quoted at 106.50 against 106.04-106.12 but dealers were unable to confirm deals.
